title: Will we soon be extinct?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a Turkish author, Harun Yahya, who offered a large cash prize for definitive fossil evidence of evolution, and use it to discuss the fossil record and creationism. They then cover a 2007 British study linking warm greenhouse climates to mass extinctions, the end-Permian extinction about 251 million years ago, and the role of biodiversity, using nitrogen cycling in soil as an example. They close with the human population bottleneck about 70,000 years ago and a joking aside about mouth breathing, concluding that a mass extinction is possible. The episode is a 2008 installment titled "Will we soon be extinct?"

segments.title: Opening banter and Turkish author
segments.summary: Hosts open the show and introduce Turkish author Harun Yahya, who offered a large sum for definitive fossil evidence of evolution. They describe his creationist views and his opposition to Richard Dawkins.

segments.title: Fossil record and intermediate forms
segments.summary: Discussion of what an intermediate fossil is and why the fossil record is spotty. They introduce the competing models of phyletic gradualism and punctuated equilibrium.

segments.title: Greenhouse periods and mass extinction
segments.summary: A British study compared the fossil record with global climate over 520 million years and found mass extinctions tended to occur in warm greenhouse periods like the present, raising the question of whether humans will soon be extinct.

segments.title: End-Permian extinction and biodiversity
segments.summary: The end-Permian extinction about 251 million years ago wiped out most species. The hosts discuss how humans would struggle without biodiversity, comparing the Earth to a machine with interdependent parts.

segments.title: Nitrogen, soil microbes and crops
segments.summary: Worms and microbes in soil produce nitrogen that feeds crops, so losing biodiversity could cause crop failure. The hosts note that humans' technology and equatorial origins may help them survive.

segments.title: Human population bottleneck
segments.summary: Humanity is thought to have passed through an evolutionary bottleneck about 70,000 years ago, when the population may have dropped to around 15,000 people, followed by a joking theory about mouth breathing.

segments.title: Conclusion and sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck concludes that a mass extinction is entirely possible. They promote the article on HowStuffWorks and invite listener email.
